Research / Adaptive intelligence

What happens as a learning
agent keeps learning?

We study the changing behavior of adaptive digital systems through evolutionary theory, probability, and computation.

All research↗

Recursive-learning bots change through repeated feedback and updates. We examine how behavior drifts, how incentives shape adaptation, and how monitoring can keep pace with an evolving system.

Questions we explore.

01

Behavioral drift

Study how behavior changes through repeated feedback, updates, and interaction.

02

Incentives & selection

Examine how competing objectives and environmental pressures shape adaptive behavior.

03

Monitoring & stability

Ask which observations reveal a changing system and when a forecast needs reassessment.

04

Higher-order evolution

Explore how the processes that generate variation and learning can themselves change over time.

Evolution beyond the living world.

Our laboratory brings evolutionary theory into conversation with artificial intelligence. First-order evolution has been compared with a “blind watchmaker.” Higher-order processes can change how variation and adaptation occur. We ask how these ideas can inform the study of systems that learn.

Biological × digital

A connected perspective.

Different mechanisms can share a common mathematical language. The distinctions matter as much as the similarities.
